parsed.impact: Cards reveal the answer and move on with a working 0.5 s guard; unit tests and Maestro flows pass in CI; only robustness nits remain (silent green when root is unavailable, locale-tag parsing, long-word sizing heuristic).

findings.text: scripts/test-acceptance.sh:171 — when `adb root` or the locale change fails, run_language_flows only says BLOCKED and `status` stays 0, so TC-03-01…05 can go unrun on a device or image where root is not available (physical device, a Play image) and yarn test:acceptance still exits 0 → fail on CI (e.g. when CI is set) or at least add a `record … fail` so the gap is visible in the exit code

scripts/test-acceptance.sh:147 — the "-LANG-rREGION-" match for `am get-config` assumes a tag with a region: a restored original of "en" (no region) builds "-en-ren-", never matches, and the restore waits 180 s then only warns; scripts with a script subtag (zh-Hans-CN) do not match either → derive the config string only from the language-region form, or compare against `getprop persist.sys.locale` / `Locale` instead of am get-config

src/app/cards/[category].tsx:28 — cardType() sizes by CHARACTER_WIDTH 0.6 of the window width and ignores the system font scale (PixelRatio.getFontScale()), the horizontal safe-area insets and wide capitals (W, Ł, Ż); a long word in capitals or at font scale >1 can still be split mid-word, because adjustsFontSizeToFit only shrinks for height, not for width → divide by the font scale and keep the heuristic documented as approximate (not blocking at default settings)

src/app/index.tsx:16 — router.push in the category Pressable has no guard, so a child's quick double touch on a category (before the new screen is drawn) can push the card screen twice, leaving two stacked cards for the later back story (US-03-04) → use router.navigate, or push once; today it is harmless because there is no back

scripts/test-acceptance.sh:408 — the locale is restored with a second framework restart (about 1 minute) and an `unroot`, also on throwaway CI emulators; it also writes persist.sys.locale where it was empty before → acceptable as written (it protects a local device); optionally skip the restore when $CI is set
